messages:
samir: Heads-up — ACME POC asked for a daily-bucket traffic model and a short note on how KV/prefix cache affects reserved GPU sizing. Also they want recommended autoscale policies for commit pricing. Any immediate blockers from security questionnaire? :coffee:

jess: Got it. Quick confirm — their current profile: ~2k concurrent, avg 15 tokens per request, 90% generation and 10% embeddings, diurnal 30% variance, and occasional 3x spike windows?

samir: Yep that's what Presales captured. They also mentioned one nightly bulk job that can run for ~10m and cause a 3x spike.

emily: Rough sketch numbers so team can pass to finance and infra: with our int8 quantized model on A100-equivalent, effective throughput ~250 tokens/s per GPU under our batching strategy. At 15 tokens/req that's ~16 req/s per GPU. For sustained 2k concurrent assuming 1s service time you'd need ~125 GPUs to handle steady rps (2000 req/s / 16 req/s per GPU ≈ 125).

emily: But this is conservative because of KV/prefix cache: if 60% of tokens hit the cache (repeated prompt prefixes), token throughput demand drops to ~40% of baseline — that reduces GPU need to ~50 GPUs for the same steady load.

emily: Proposed reserve policy: reserve 60 GPUs (covers steady with moderate cache hit and leaves room for degradation). Configure autoscale to add burst pool up to 180 GPUs for 3x spikes (fast scale up with prewarmed slots). Keep reserved = baseline * 0.9 for SLA headroom and prewarm 20% of burst capacity for sub-10s scale-up.

jess: Can we express that to finance as two scenarios: (A) baseline with 60 reserved GPUs (expected unit cost X) and (B) conservative reserve 125 GPUs (higher cost but no burst dependency). They want the monthly delta.

emily: Yes. I'll produce a quick cost delta sheet. Also add quantization sensitivity: if they accept int4 we can halve GPU count in many workloads — call that optional savings.

raj: Security checklist: they marked KMS/HSM, VPC peering, and audit logs as must-haves. Private deployment is on the table if the SOC2 questionnaire flags anything. For reserved capacity we need to confirm key rotation policy and whether logs must be forwarded to their Splunk instance. If they require on-prem, cost & lead times change.

samir: Good note. @raj can you flag which questionnaire answers would force Private vs Hosted? We need a clean handoff in the doc.

raj: Short answer: if they require customer-managed keys (HSM) + no egress of tokenized data out of their VPC => Private. If they accept our KMS with customer CMKs and strict VPC peering then Hosted Dedicated is OK. I'll mark the specific Qs in the questionnaire with a red/green indicator.

jess: Operational question: how fast can burst pool spin up? We promised sub-30s in past decks with prewarmed slots. Ops? @ops-bot any constraints on AZ warmup times?

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Prewarm policy currently supports N prewarmed slots per AZ. Typical cold->ready time for new GPU workers is ~18-45s depending on image pull and kernel compile. We recommend prewarming 20% of burst as emily suggested to keep scale-up <15s for common spikes.

emily: For the handoff doc to sales/finance include three figures: steady-state reserved GPUs (60), burst ceiling (180), and fallback (125 reserved if they want no burst dependency). Also include cache hit sensitivity: 30/60/80% cache hit scenarios and resulting reserved counts.

samir: Perfect. I'll update the pricing sheet and draft a short note to include in the security answers: private if HSM+no-egress, otherwise hosted dedicated with CMKs and VPC peering.

jess: I'll schedule a 30-min POC sync with ACME and invite security and infra to walk through the runway and prewarm plan. Prefer tomorrow 10am PT.

samir: Thanks — please include the cost delta and the 'what forces private' bullets. That should unblock legal/finance. :thumbsup:
